title: 新朋友
body:
你好！我叫小明。今天我去公园，看见一个男孩。他说："你好，我叫大伟。"我说："你好，大伟！我们做朋友吧。"大伟笑了，说："好！"

我们一起去吃饭。大伟吃米饭，我吃面条。我很渴，想要喝水。大伟给我一瓶水，说："给你。"我说："谢谢！"我们很高兴，一起说："我们是好朋友！"
translation: Hello! My name is Xiaoming. Today I went to the park and saw a boy. He said, "Hello, my name is Dawei." I said, "Hello, Dawei! Let's be friends." Dawei smiled and said, "Okay!"

We went to eat together. Dawei ate rice, I ate noodles. I was very thirsty and wanted to drink water. Dawei gave me a bottle of water and said, "Here you are." I said, "Thank you!" We were very happy and said together, "We are good friends!"

title: 朋友的家
body:
你好！我是小明。今天我去朋友家玩。我的朋友叫小红，她很好。她给我水喝，还给我吃的。我说：“谢谢！”我们吃苹果，很开心。

下午，我们一起看书。小红说：“你喜欢喝水吗？”我说：“喜欢，谢谢！”我们笑了很多。晚上我回家，今天真好！
translation: Hello! I am Xiaoming. Today I went to my friend's house to play. My friend is called Xiaohong, she is very nice. She gave me water to drink, and also gave me food to eat. I said: "Thank you!" We ate apples and were very happy.
In the afternoon, we read books together. Xiaohong said: "Do you like to drink water?" I said: "Yes, thank you!" We laughed a lot. In the evening I went home, today was really good!

title: 新的工作机会
body:
小王在一家小公司工作了三年，积累了很多经验。有一天，他的朋友说有一家大公司正在找人，那里的工作环境非常好。小王听了以后，决定去参加面试。

面试那天，小王和经理讨论了以前的工作。经理给了他一个建议，说他的经验很适合这个新职位。小王觉得这是一个很好的机会，心里很高兴。他想了想，决定接受这个工作。

一个月后，小王搬到了新城市。虽然离开了老朋友，但他不后悔自己的决定。新的环境让他学到了更多东西，他每天都过得很充实。
translation: Xiao Wang had worked at a small company for three years and accumulated a lot of experience. One day, his friend told him that a large company was hiring and the working environment there was very good. After hearing this, Xiao Wang decided to go for an interview.

On the day of the interview, Xiao Wang discussed his previous work with the manager. The manager gave him a suggestion, saying that his experience was very suitable for this new position. Xiao Wang felt this was a great opportunity and was very happy. After thinking it over, he decided to accept the job.

A month later, Xiao Wang moved to a new city. Although he left his old friends behind, he did not regret his decision. The new environment allowed him to learn more things, and he lived a fulfilling life every day.

title: 新工作的第一天
body:
小李去年大学毕业，一直在找合适的工作。上个月，他终于得到一个机会，去一家环保公司面试。面试时，经理问他有没有相关经验，小李诚实地说自己刚毕业，经验不多，但愿意学习。经理觉得他的态度很好，决定给他这个工作。

上班第一天，小李发现办公室的环境非常好，有很多绿色植物，阳光也很充足。同事们都很友好，中午大家一起吃饭，讨论公司的新项目。一位老员工给了小李一个建议：每天早到十分钟，可以更好地准备一天的工作。小李觉得这个建议很有用，决定以后每天都这样做。

三个月后，小李已经习惯了新工作。他感谢那次面试的机会，也感谢同事们的帮助。现在他有了一些工作经验，也开始帮助新来的同事。他觉得，好的工作环境和善良的人，让每一天都很开心。
translation: Xiao Li graduated from university last year and had been looking for a suitable job. Last month, he finally got an opportunity to interview at an environmental protection company. During the interview, the manager asked if he had any relevant experience. Xiao Li honestly said he had just graduated and didn't have much experience, but he was willing to learn. The manager thought his attitude was good and decided to give him the job.

On his first day of work, Xiao Li discovered that the office environment was very nice, with many green plants and plenty of sunlight. His colleagues were all very friendly. At noon, everyone ate together and discussed the company's new projects. An experienced employee gave Xiao Li a suggestion: arrive ten minutes early every day to better prepare for the day's work. Xiao Li thought this suggestion was very useful and decided to do this every day from now on.

Three months later, Xiao Li had already gotten used to his new job. He was grateful for that interview opportunity and also grateful for his colleagues' help. Now he had some work experience and had started helping new colleagues. He felt that a good work environment and kind people made every day very happy.

title: 并购风云
body:
林氏集团的年轻CEO林薇坐在会议室里，面前摆着两家科技公司的收购方案。她深知这次决策关系到集团未来十年的发展，必须制定一个长远的战略。她的助理递来一杯咖啡，轻声提醒对方谈判代表已经在隔壁等候。

第一家公司的创始人是个固执的工程师，谈判持续了六个小时仍毫无进展。对方拒绝在任何核心技术上让步，林薇意识到这场交易注定无法达成。她果断终止了谈判，转而全力争取第二家初创企业。这家公司的AI算法虽然尚不成熟，但她敏锐地发现了其中蕴藏的巨大潜力。

与第二家公司的谈判同样艰难。创始人团队坚持要保持独立运营，不愿完全并入集团。林薇彻夜权衡利弊，最终在关键条款上做出了妥协——她同意保留对方的品牌名称和研发团队，换取核心技术的独家授权。这个决定让董事会颇有微词，但她相信自己的判断。

三年后，那家被收购的AI公司成长为行业独角兽，为林氏集团带来了数百亿的市值增长。当初质疑她的人不得不承认，正是那次明智的妥协与精准的战略眼光，让集团在人工智能浪潮中占据了先机。林薇站在落地窗前，看着城市的灯火，想起了那个漫长的谈判之夜。
translation: Lin Wei, the young CEO of Lin Group, sat in the conference room with acquisition proposals from two tech companies on her desk. She knew this decision would determine the group's development over the next decade, so she had to formulate a long-term strategy. Her assistant brought her a cup of coffee and quietly reminded her that the negotiation representatives were waiting next door.

The founder of the first company was a stubborn engineer, and after six hours of negotiation there was still no progress. The other party refused to make any concessions on core technology, and Lin Wei realized this deal was destined to fail. She decisively terminated the negotiation and turned her full attention to acquiring the second startup. Although this company's AI algorithms were still immature, she keenly sensed the enormous potential hidden within.

The negotiation with the second company was equally difficult. The founding team insisted on maintaining independent operations and was unwilling to fully merge into the group. Lin Wei spent the entire night weighing the pros and cons, and finally made a compromise on key terms—she agreed to keep their brand name and R&D team in exchange for exclusive licensing of their core technology. This decision drew considerable criticism from the board, but she trusted her own judgment.

Three years later, that acquired AI company grew into an industry unicorn, bringing tens of billions in market value growth to Lin Group. Those who had questioned her at the time had to admit that it was precisely that wise compromise and precise strategic vision that allowed the group to seize the initiative in the artificial intelligence wave. Lin Wei stood before the floor-to-ceiling windows, looking at the city lights, and thought of that long night of negotiation.

title: 谈判桌上的博弈
body:
林氏集团的CEO林远正面临一场关键的谈判。一家国际科技公司希望收购他辛苦创立的人工智能企业，但对方开出的条件远低于他的预期。会议室里，双方代表各执一词，气氛紧张。林远深知，这不仅是价格的较量，更是战略的比拼。他必须让对方看到公司的真正潜力，而不是急于妥协。

经过三天的拉锯，林远决定改变策略。他不再被动防守，而是主动展示公司自主研发的核心算法，以及在医疗诊断领域的突破性应用。他用数据证明，这家企业未来的市场价值至少翻三倍。对方代表开始认真权衡利弊，意识到低估报价可能错失良机。

深夜的谈判进入最后阶段。林远提出一个创新方案：部分股权交换，保留核心技术团队，同时获得对方的全球渠道资源。这是一个需要双方妥协的架构，但他相信只有双赢才能长久。经过反复讨论，对方终于点头。签字前，林远最后一次审视合同条款，确认每一个细节都符合最初的战略目标。

三个月后，合并后的新公司上市首日股价大涨。林远在采访中感慨，那次谈判教会他最重要的一课：真正的成功不在于谁占上风，而在于能否在复杂局面中找到平衡点。如今他常对年轻创业者说，学会权衡与妥协，才能释放最大的潜力。
translation: Lin Yuan, CEO of Lin Group, was facing a crucial negotiation. An international tech company wanted to acquire his AI enterprise, but their offer fell far below his expectations. In the conference room, both sides held firm, the atmosphere tense. Lin Yuan knew this was not merely a battle over price, but a contest of strategy. He had to make the other side see his company's true potential rather than rushing to compromise.

After three days of stalemate, Lin Yuan decided to change tactics. Instead of passive defense, he proactively showcased the company's self-developed core algorithms and breakthrough applications in medical diagnostics. He used data to prove the enterprise's market value would triple in the future. The other side's representatives began carefully weighing the pros and cons, realizing their underestimated offer might cost them a golden opportunity.

The late-night negotiations entered their final phase. Lin Yuan proposed an innovative solution: partial equity exchange, keeping the core technical team intact while gaining access to the other party's global distribution channels. This was a structure requiring compromise from both sides, but he believed only mutual benefit could last. After repeated discussion, the other side finally agreed. Before signing, Lin Yuan reviewed the contract terms one last time, confirming every detail aligned with his original strategic goals.

Three months later, the merged company's stock soared on its first day of trading. Reflecting in an interview, Lin Yuan said that negotiation taught him the most important lesson: true success lies not in who gains the upper hand, but in finding balance amid complexity. Now he often tells young entrepreneurs that learning to weigh trade-offs and compromise is how one unleashes maximum potential.

title: 两家公司的合并之路
body:
张明是一家科技公司的CEO，最近他一直在思考公司的未来战略。市场竞争越来越激烈，他意识到单靠自己的力量很难突破瓶颈。经过深思熟虑，他决定寻找一家有潜力的初创企业进行合作。

在谈判桌上，张明遇到了年轻的创始人李华。李华的公司虽然规模不大，但在人工智能领域有着独特的技术优势。双方就股权分配和管理架构展开了激烈的讨论，谁也不肯轻易让步。

经过连续三天的交锋，张明开始认真权衡各种方案的利弊。他明白，如果过于坚持己见，合作很可能破裂。最终，他选择做出妥协，同意让李华保留更多的决策权，以换取对方核心技术的长期授权。

这次成功的合作让两家公司都获得了新的发展机遇。张明常常感慨，真正的商业智慧不在于赢得每一场争论，而在于懂得何时该坚持、何时该退让。这种灵活的权衡之道，正是企业长久发展的关键所在。
translation: Zhang Ming is the CEO of a technology company. Recently, he has been contemplating his company's future strategy. Market competition has become increasingly fierce, and he realized that relying solely on his own strength would make it difficult to break through bottlenecks. After careful consideration, he decided to seek cooperation with a promising startup.

At the negotiation table, Zhang Ming met the young founder Li Hua. Although Li Hua's company was not large in scale, it possessed unique technical advantages in the field of artificial intelligence. Both sides engaged in intense discussions regarding equity distribution and management structure, with neither willing to easily give way.

After three consecutive days of confrontation, Zhang Ming began to carefully weigh the pros and cons of various proposals. He understood that if he insisted too stubbornly on his own views, the cooperation would likely fall apart. In the end, he chose to make a compromise, agreeing to let Li Hua retain more decision-making power in exchange for long-term licensing of the other party's core technology.

This successful cooperation brought new development opportunities to both companies. Zhang Ming often reflects that true business wisdom lies not in winning every argument, but in knowing when to persist and when to yield. This flexible approach to weighing trade-offs is precisely the key to long-term enterprise development.

title: 小李的银行实习
body:
小李刚从大学毕业，在一家银行找到了实习工作。第一天上班，他穿了一件很重的西装，因为妈妈说他看起来会更成熟。可是地铁上的人太多，他差点迟到，心里还想着会不会给同事留下不好的印象。

他的主管是一位长头发的女经理，她让小李重复核对每一份文件，不能有任何差错。小李工作很认真，但中午发现自己的钱包不见了，可能是挤地铁时掉了。他很难过，觉得这一天真是差极了，连午饭钱都没有。

下午，一位好心的同事借给他钱吃饭，还安慰他说每个人都会遇到困难。小李决定明天早点出门，不再穿那么重的衣服。虽然今天很糟糕，但他学到了很多，也交到了新朋友。他相信以后一定会越来越好的。
translation: Xiao Li had just graduated from university and found an internship at a bank. On his first day of work, he wore a very heavy suit because his mother said he would look more mature. However, there were too many people on the subway, and he almost arrived late, still worrying about whether he would leave a bad impression on his colleagues.

His supervisor was a female manager with long hair. She asked Xiao Li to repeatedly check every document, and there could not be any mistakes. Xiao Li worked very seriously, but at noon he discovered his wallet was missing—probably lost while squeezing onto the subway. He was very sad, feeling that this day was simply terrible, and he didn't even have money for lunch.

In the afternoon, a kind colleague lent him money for lunch and comforted him by saying everyone encounters difficulties. Xiao Li decided to leave home earlier tomorrow and not wear such heavy clothes anymore. Although today was very bad, he learned a lot and made new friends. He believed that things would definitely get better and better in the future.

title: 小王的双语难题
body:
小王在市中心的一家银行工作，每天都很忙。他从小就想成为一名翻译，所以大学时学了两门外语。现在他的工作虽然稳定，但离梦想还很远。他常常问自己：还要等多久才能改变呢？

去年，公司派他去国外出差。那次的任务很重，他不仅要参加会议，还要负责整理很多文件。有一次，他把一份合同看错了，差点让公司损失很多钱。老板让他重新检查一遍，他只好重做一次。虽然很累，但他学到了很多经验，也发现自己的外语水平还差得远。

回国后，小王决定每天早起学习。他相信只要坚持，梦想就会慢慢长大。现在他不再抱怨工作，而是把银行的工作当成练习的机会。他相信，总有一天，他能成为一名优秀的翻译。
translation: Xiao Wang works at a bank in the city center and is busy every day. Since childhood, he wanted to become a translator, so he studied two foreign languages in college. Now his job is stable, but still far from his dream. He often asks himself: how much longer does he still have to wait to change?

Last year, the company sent him on a business trip abroad. That assignment was heavy; he not only had to attend meetings but also organize many documents. Once, he misread a contract and almost caused the company to lose a lot of money. His boss made him check it again, so he had to repeat the work. Although very tired, he learned a lot of experience and also realized his foreign language level was still far from enough.

After returning to China, Xiao Wang decided to get up early every day to study. He believes that as long as he persists, his dream will gradually grow. Now he no longer complains about work; instead, he treats his bank job as an opportunity to practice. He believes that one day, he will become an excellent translator.

title: 银行里的老朋友
body:
老王在银行工作了二十年，每天看着窗外的树慢慢长高了。他虽然年纪大了，但还很喜欢这份工作。有一天，一位老朋友来找他，说要还一笔多年前的钱。

"这笔钱我差太久了，"老朋友不好意思地说，"现在终于能还给你。"老王笑着摇头说："不用还了，当年你帮我的时候，我从没让你写借条。"老朋友坚持要把钱放下，说这份情谊太重，不能不还。老王只好收下，但心里决定把这些钱捐给山区的孩子。

后来，老王被公司差去山区检查新项目。他看到孩子们用那笔钱买了书，脸上露出笑容。回城后，他给老朋友写了一封长信，又把这段经历讲给银行里的年轻同事听。大家都觉得，真正的友谊不是钱能衡量的，但用心还的情谊，会让美好事情重新发生。
translation: Lao Wang had worked at the bank for twenty years, watching the trees outside the window slowly grow taller. Although he was getting older, he still loved this job very much. One day, an old friend came to see him, saying he wanted to return some money from many years ago.

"I owed this money for too long," the old friend said embarrassedly. "Now I can finally return it to you." Lao Wang smiled and shook his head, saying, "No need to return it. When you helped me back then, I never asked you to write an IOU." The old friend insisted on leaving the money, saying this friendship was too heavy not to repay. Lao Wang had no choice but to accept it, but decided in his heart to donate this money to children in the mountains.

Later, Lao Wang was dispatched by the company to the mountains to inspect a new project. He saw the children using that money to buy books, smiles on their faces. After returning to the city, he wrote a long letter to his old friend, and also told this experience to young colleagues at the bank. Everyone felt that true friendship cannot be measured by money, but heartfelt repayment allows beautiful things to happen again.

title: 雨中的邂逅
body:
你站在图书馆门口，望着外面越下越大的雨，心里有些焦急。今天是你和老朋友约定见面的日子，可这场突如其来的暴雨让交通几乎瘫痪。你踌躇着要不要冒雨冲出去，手机却突然响了——是一个陌生号码。

电话那头传来熟悉又陌生的声音："是你吗？我是林涛，我们在大学辩论赛上见过。"你愣住了，那是十年前的事了。原来他正好在附近咖啡馆避雨，透过玻璃窗看到了踌躇不定的你。这场意外的邂逅让你们都笑了起来，仿佛时光从未流逝。

你们坐在咖啡馆里，从往事聊到近况。窗外的雨渐渐小了，水洼里倒映着路灯的光。你们约定以后不再让缘分只靠偶然，要常联系。分别时，你望着他的背影，心想有些相遇真是命中注定。
translation: You stood at the library entrance, looking at the increasingly heavy rain outside, feeling somewhat anxious. Today was the day you had arranged to meet an old friend, but this sudden downpour had almost paralyzed the traffic. You hesitated about whether to rush out into the rain, when your phone suddenly rang—it was an unfamiliar number.

On the other end of the line came a voice that was both familiar and strange: "Is that you? I'm Lin Tao, we met at the university debate competition." You were stunned—that was ten years ago. It turned out he happened to be taking shelter from the rain at a nearby café, and through the glass window had seen you hesitating. This unexpected chance encounter made you both laugh, as if time had never passed.

You sat in the café, chatting from old memories to recent situations. The rain outside gradually lightened, and puddles reflected the streetlights. You agreed that you would no longer leave your connection to chance alone, and would keep in touch more often. When parting, you watched his retreating figure and thought to yourself that some meetings are truly destined.

title: 雨中的邂逅
body:
你站在咖啡馆的门口，望着窗外突如其来的大雨，心里有些踌躇。三年前，你最好的朋友去了南方，你们渐渐失去了联系。今天，你原本只是想独自喝杯咖啡，却没想到会在这里遇见她。

就在你犹豫要不要冲进雨里的时候，一个熟悉的身影推门而入。那是你的朋友！她的头发被雨水打湿，脸上却带着惊喜的笑容。原来，她上周刚搬回这座城市，今天也是偶然路过这家咖啡馆。这场意外的邂逅让你们都激动得说不出话来。

你们点了热茶，坐在窗边聊了很久。她说南方的气候太潮湿，她想念这里的四季分明。你笑着说，刚才你还在踌躇要不要离开，现在看来，这场雨是老天送给你们的礼物。你们约定以后每周都见面，再也不让距离冲淡友谊。窗外的雨渐渐小了，而你们的心里却充满了温暖。
translation: You stood at the door of the café, looking at the sudden heavy rain outside, feeling somewhat hesitant. Three years ago, your best friend went to the south, and you gradually lost contact. Today, you had only wanted to drink coffee alone, never expecting to meet her here.

Just as you were hesitating whether to rush into the rain, a familiar figure pushed open the door. It was your friend! Her hair was wet from the rain, yet her face carried a surprised smile. It turned out she had just moved back to this city last week, and today she too had happened to pass by this café. This unexpected chance encounter left you both too excited to speak.

You ordered hot tea and sat by the window chatting for a long time. She said the climate in the south was too humid, and she missed the distinct four seasons here. You smiled and said that just now you were still hesitating whether to leave; now it seemed this rain was a gift from heaven to you both. You agreed to meet every week from now on, never letting distance dilute your friendship again. The rain outside gradually lightened, while your hearts were full of warmth.

title: 雨中的邂逅
body:
去年夏天，我在江南的一座小镇旅行。那天下午突然下起了大雨，我匆忙躲进一家老茶馆，浑身都被雨水打湿了。正当我捧着热茶取暖时，忽然看见一个熟悉的身影——那竟是我多年未见的老朋友小林。我们相视一笑，这场意外的邂逅让寒冷的雨天变得温暖起来。

小林告诉我，他来这里是为了处理一些工作，原本打算第二天就离开。我们聊了很久，从过去的校园生活聊到各自的工作。然而，当我邀请他共进晚餐时，他却踌躇了片刻，说晚上还有一个重要的视频会议。我能看出他眼中的歉意，便不再勉强。

分别时，小林递给我一张名片，说下次来北京一定要联系他。我接过名片，发现上面印着某科技公司的CEO头衔。原来这些年他发展得这么好，我真心为他感到高兴。雨渐渐停了，我们约定明年春天再见面，然后各自走向不同的方向。
translation: Last summer, I was traveling in a small town in Jiangnan. That afternoon, it suddenly started raining heavily, and I hurried into an old teahouse, completely soaked by the rain. Just as I was warming myself with hot tea, I suddenly saw a familiar figure—it was actually my old friend Xiao Lin whom I hadn't seen for many years. We smiled at each other, and this unexpected encounter made the cold rainy day feel warm.

Xiao Lin told me he had come here to take care of some work and had originally planned to leave the next day. We chatted for a long time, from our past school days to our respective jobs. However, when I invited him to dinner, he hesitated for a moment, saying he had an important video conference that evening. I could see the apology in his eyes and didn't insist further.

When parting, Xiao Lin handed me a business card, saying I must contact him next time I came to Beijing. I took the card and found it bore the title of CEO of a technology company. So he had developed so well all these years—I was truly happy for him. The rain gradually stopped, we agreed to meet again next spring, and then walked in different directions.

title: 延误的航班
body:
去年夏天，我们一家四口决定去云南旅行。爸爸提前两个月就开始计划这次旅行，妈妈负责预订酒店和机票，我和弟弟则忙着查攻略，看看哪里有好吃的和好玩的。

出发那天早上，天气特别好，阳光明媚，一点也没有要下雨的样子。我们早早地把行李收拾好，每个人都带了一个大箱子，里面装满了衣服和日用品。我还特意留了一些空间，准备装纪念品回来送给朋友。

到了机场，我们办好了登机手续，通过了安检，在候机厅里等着。爸爸看了看手表说："还有两个小时，我们可以慢慢等。"妈妈却有点担心，因为她听说这几天那边天气不太好。

果然，广播里突然传来消息：由于目的地机场大雾，我们的航班延误了，起飞时间待定。听到这个消息，弟弟立刻哭了起来，因为他特别期待这次旅行。爸爸安慰他说："没关系，延误是常有的事，我们耐心等等。"

这一等就是六个小时。我们在机场吃了午饭，又吃了晚饭，把带来的零食都吃完了。妈妈不停地给导游打电话，告诉他我们可能会晚到，请他帮忙调整行程。导游很理解，说他会先安排其他客人，让我们到了再联系他。

晚上九点，飞机终于起飞了。到达云南的时候已经是深夜，我们累极了，但酒店的工作人员还在等着我们。爸爸不好意思地说："真是抱歉，航班延误太久了。"工作人员笑着说："没关系，这里的风景值得等待。"

第二天醒来，阳光照进窗户，外面的风景美得让我们忘记了昨天的疲惫。青山绿水的，空气也特别清新。导游准时来接我们，还给我们带了当地的特色早餐。他说："你们虽然来得晚，但正好错过了昨天的大雨，今天天气最适合看风景。"

接下来的几天，我们玩得很开心。我们去了古城，买了好多纪念品，有手工银饰、茶叶和漂亮的围巾。妈妈本来很担心预算不够，因为航班延误让我们多花了机场吃饭的钱，但爸爸说："旅行最重要的是开心，钱的事情回去再说。"

最后一天，我们在机场等返程航班的时候，弟弟突然说："虽然第一天延误了那么久，但我觉得这次旅行还是很好。"我们都笑了。是啊，计划永远赶不上变化，但只要一家人在一起，什么困难都能变成美好的回忆。
translation: Last summer, our family of four decided to travel to Yunnan. Dad started planning this trip two months in advance, Mom was responsible for booking hotels and flights, and my brother and I were busy looking up travel guides to see where there was good food and fun things to do.

On the morning of departure, the weather was particularly nice, with bright sunshine and no sign of rain. We packed our luggage early, each bringing a large suitcase full of clothes and daily necessities. I also deliberately left some space to bring back souvenirs for my friends.

When we arrived at the airport, we checked in, passed through security, and waited in the departure lounge. Dad looked at his watch and said, 'We still have two hours, we can wait slowly.' But Mom was a bit worried because she had heard that the weather there hadn't been very good these past few days.

Sure enough, an announcement suddenly came over the loudspeaker: due to heavy fog at the destination airport, our flight was delayed, and the departure time was to be determined. Hearing this news, my brother immediately started crying because he had been especially looking forward to this trip. Dad comforted him, saying, 'It's okay, delays are common, let's wait patiently.'

We ended up waiting for six hours. We ate lunch at the airport, then dinner, and finished all the snacks we had brought. Mom kept calling the tour guide to tell him we might arrive late and asked him to help adjust the itinerary. The tour guide was very understanding and said he would arrange for other guests first and told us to contact him when we arrived.

At nine in the evening, the plane finally took off. When we arrived in Yunnan, it was already late at night. We were exhausted, but the hotel staff was still waiting for us. Dad said apologetically, 'I'm really sorry, the flight was delayed for so long.' The staff member smiled and said, 'It's okay, the scenery here is worth waiting for.'

When we woke up the next day, sunlight streamed through the window, and the scenery outside was so beautiful that we forgot yesterday's fatigue. There were green mountains and clear water, and the air was especially fresh. The tour guide came to pick us up on time and even brought us local specialty breakfast. He said, 'Although you arrived late, you just missed yesterday's heavy rain. Today's weather is the best for sightseeing.'

In the following days, we had a wonderful time. We visited the ancient town and bought many souvenirs, including handmade silver jewelry, tea, and beautiful scarves. Mom had originally been worried that the budget wouldn't be enough because the flight delay caused us to spend extra money on airport meals, but Dad said, 'The most important thing about travel is being happy. We'll worry about money when we get back.'

On the last day, as we were waiting for our return flight at the airport, my brother suddenly said, 'Even though we were delayed for so long on the first day, I still think this trip was great.' We all laughed. Yes, plans can never keep up with changes, but as long as the family is together, any difficulty can become a beautiful memory.

title: 延误的航班
body:
去年夏天，我们一家人计划了一次去云南的旅行。爸爸提前三个月就预订了机票和酒店，妈妈则仔细计算了预算，确保每一分钱都花在值得的地方。我和弟弟都很兴奋，每天都在想象那里的美丽风景。

出发那天早上，天气看起来不太好，天空布满了灰色的云。爸爸安慰我们说，夏天的雨来得快，去得也快，不会影响我们的行程。我们带着满满的行李，里面装着送给亲戚的礼物和我们需要的衣服，早早地赶到了机场。

在机场，我们顺利地通过了安检。妈妈反复检查护照和登机牌，生怕遗漏了什么重要文件。我和弟弟则在候机厅里跑来跑去，看着窗外的飞机起飞降落，心里充满了期待。导游已经在目的地等着我们了，她发短信说会带我们看最美的风景。

然而，就在登机前三十分钟，广播里突然传来消息：由于天气原因，我们的航班延误了。工作人员没有告诉我们具体要等多久，只是让大家耐心等待。爸爸皱起了眉头，因为这意味着我们的计划可能会被打乱。

妈妈立刻打开手机，查看其他航班的信息，但当天的机票都已经卖完了。我们只好坐在椅子上等待，行李堆在身边，像一座小山。弟弟开始抱怨，说早知道就带更多的零食来。我则担心导游会不会一直等我们，毕竟我们已经付了定金。

三个小时过去了，天气依然没有好转。机场里的商店成了我们的消遣地方，妈妈给我和弟弟各买了一个小纪念品，是一只陶瓷做的孔雀，代表着云南的特色。她说，虽然航班延误让人心烦，但一家人在一起就是最好的旅行。

终于，在傍晚时分，雨停了，我们的航班可以起飞了。虽然比原计划晚了五个小时，但我们还是登上了飞机。透过窗户，我看到了美丽的晚霞，红色的云朵像燃烧的火焰。那一刻，我觉得所有的等待都是值得的。

到达云南时，已经是深夜。导游果然还在机场等着我们，她笑着说："航班延误是常有的事，重要的是你们安全到了。"她帮我们安排了住宿，并告诉我们明天的行程会稍微调整，但所有预订的项目都不会少。

这次旅行让我明白，计划永远赶不上变化。即使遇到航班延误这样的麻烦，只要家人在一起，保持好心情，依然可以看到最美的风景，买到最有意义的纪念品。预算可能会因为额外的餐费而超支，但这些意外的经历，反而成了我们最珍贵的回忆。
translation: Last summer, our whole family planned a trip to Yunnan. Dad booked the flights and hotel three months in advance, while Mom carefully calculated the budget to make sure every penny was spent on something worthwhile. My younger brother and I were both very excited, imagining the beautiful scenery there every day.

On the morning of departure, the weather didn't look good—the sky was covered with gray clouds. Dad comforted us by saying that summer rain comes quickly and leaves quickly, so it wouldn't affect our trip. We brought full luggage containing gifts for relatives and the clothes we needed, and arrived at the airport early.

At the airport, we passed through security smoothly. Mom repeatedly checked our passports and boarding passes, afraid of missing any important documents. My brother and I ran around the waiting hall, watching planes take off and land through the windows, our hearts full of anticipation. The tour guide was already waiting for us at the destination and sent a text saying she would show us the most beautiful scenery.

However, just thirty minutes before boarding, an announcement suddenly came over the loudspeaker: due to weather conditions, our flight was delayed. The staff didn't tell us exactly how long we would have to wait, only asking everyone to be patient. Dad frowned, because this meant our plans might be disrupted.

Mom immediately opened her phone to check information about other flights, but tickets for that day were already sold out. We had no choice but to sit in our chairs and wait, with our luggage piled beside us like a small mountain. My brother started complaining, saying he wished he had brought more snacks. I worried whether the tour guide would keep waiting for us, since we had already paid the deposit.

Three hours passed, and the weather still hadn't improved. The shops in the airport became our place to pass the time. Mom bought each of us a small souvenir—a ceramic peacock representing Yunnan's special characteristics. She said that although the flight delay was frustrating, being together as a family was the best kind of travel.

Finally, in the evening, the rain stopped and our flight could depart. Although it was five hours later than originally planned, we still boarded the plane. Through the window, I saw the beautiful sunset glow, with red clouds like burning flames. At that moment, I felt that all the waiting had been worth it.

When we arrived in Yunnan, it was already late at night. The tour guide was indeed still waiting for us at the airport. She smiled and said, "Flight delays happen all the time; what matters is that you arrived safely." She helped us arrange our accommodation and told us that tomorrow's itinerary would be slightly adjusted, but all the booked activities would remain.

This trip taught me that plans can never keep up with changes. Even when encountering troubles like flight delays, as long as the family is together and keeps a good mood, you can still see the most beautiful scenery and buy the most meaningful souvenirs. The budget might be exceeded due to extra meal expenses, but these unexpected experiences became our most precious memories instead.

title: 延误的航班
body:
去年夏天，我们全家计划了一次去云南的旅行。爸爸提前三个月就预订好了机票和酒店，妈妈认真地做了详细的旅行计划，连每天吃什么、买什么纪念品都想好了。我和弟弟特别期待，因为这是我们第一次全家一起出远门。

出发那天，我们凌晨四点就起床了。爸爸检查了三遍护照，妈妈把行李收拾得整整齐齐，连雨伞和防晒霜都带了。我们打车去机场，一路上有说有笑，想象着云南美丽的风景。

到了机场，我们顺利办好了登机手续。导游已经在群里发了消息，说会在目的地接我们。我们坐在候机厅里，吃着妈妈准备的早餐，心情特别好。我看着窗外的飞机，心想再过几个小时就能看到雪山了。

可是，广播突然响了："各位乘客，由于天气原因，飞往昆明的航班将延误四个小时。"我们一下子愣住了。爸爸赶紧去问工作人员，得到的回答是一样的——天气不好，为了安全，只能等。

四个小时！我们的计划全乱了。导游打电话来说，如果下午才到，今天安排的景点就来不及看了。妈妈算了一下，这样不仅会浪费一天的酒店钱，还会影响后面的整个行程。我们的预算本来就很紧张，现在更麻烦了。

弟弟开始哭闹，说不想等了。爸爸虽然也很着急，但还是安慰我们说："旅行中总会遇到意外，重要的是我们在一起。"妈妈想了想，决定利用这段时间，带我们去机场的书店逛逛。她给我买了一本关于云南风景的画册，给弟弟买了一个飞机模型。

中午，天气终于好转了。我们登上飞机时，大家都松了一口气。虽然延误了很久，但空姐的服务特别好，还多发了一份点心。我和弟弟看着窗外的白云，又兴奋起来。

到达昆明时，导游举着牌子在出口等我们。她笑着说："没关系，我帮你们调整了明天的行程，保证让你们看到最美的风景。"原来她早就帮我们想好了办法，还推荐了几家便宜又好吃的餐厅，帮我们省了钱。

这次旅行虽然开头不顺利，但我们看到了壮观的石林，爬上了雄伟的玉龙雪山，还买了很多漂亮的纪念品。回家以后，爸爸常说，那次延误教会了我们一件事：计划再完美，也要学会面对变化。而一家人在一起，就是最好的旅行。
translation: Last summer, our whole family planned a trip to Yunnan. Dad booked the flights and hotel three months in advance, and Mom carefully made a detailed travel plan, even thinking through what we'd eat each day and what souvenirs to buy. My younger brother and I were especially excited because this was our first time traveling far away together as a family.

On the day of departure, we woke up at four in the morning. Dad checked our passports three times, and Mom packed the luggage neatly, even bringing umbrellas and sunscreen. We took a taxi to the airport, chatting and laughing along the way, imagining Yunnan's beautiful scenery.

Arriving at the airport, we smoothly completed check-in. The tour guide had already sent a message in the group chat saying she would pick us up at our destination. We sat in the waiting hall eating the breakfast Mom had prepared, feeling wonderful. I looked at the planes outside the window, thinking that in just a few hours I would see snow-capped mountains.

But suddenly an announcement came: "Dear passengers, due to weather conditions, the flight to Kunming will be delayed by four hours." We were stunned. Dad hurried to ask the staff, and got the same answer—the weather was bad, and for safety, we could only wait.

Four hours! Our plans were completely disrupted. The tour guide called to say that if we arrived in the afternoon, we wouldn't have time for today's arranged attractions. Mom calculated that this would not only waste a day's hotel money but also affect the entire itinerary. Our budget was already tight, and now it was even more troublesome.

My brother started crying, saying he didn't want to wait anymore. Although Dad was also anxious, he comforted us by saying, "There will always be surprises in travel; what matters is that we're together." Mom thought for a moment and decided to use this time to take us to the airport bookstore. She bought me a picture book about Yunnan's scenery and bought my brother a model airplane.

By noon, the weather had finally improved. When we boarded the plane, everyone breathed a sigh of relief. Although the delay was long, the flight attendant's service was especially good, and they even gave us an extra snack. My brother and I looked at the white clouds outside the window and got excited again.

When we arrived in Kunming, the tour guide was waiting at the exit holding a sign. She smiled and said, "It's fine, I've adjusted tomorrow's itinerary for you, guaranteeing you'll see the most beautiful scenery." It turned out she had already figured out a solution for us, and even recommended several cheap and delicious restaurants to help us save money.

Although this trip didn't start smoothly, we saw the magnificent Stone Forest, climbed the majestic Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, and bought many beautiful souvenirs. After returning home, Dad often said that the delay taught us one thing: no matter how perfect the plan, you must learn to face changes. And being together as a family is the best kind of travel.

title: 柏林的夏天
body:
王磊是一名中国移民，三年前特意搬到德国学习社会学。他的口语能力不错，但阅读能力还需要提高。身边的朋友们常说德国社会很"洋气"，他却觉得理论太多、实践太少。

一天，他在图书馆看到一本关于东德历史的书。书中提到，当年有人因为反抗政府而被关进监狱，没有任何合法理由。更让他惊讶的是，书中说当时的污染问题很严重，河水难看极了，但官方却用表情包式的宣传掩盖真相。

王磊忍不住在讨论课上怼了教授："这种个人主义带来的自由，难道不是另一种暴力吗？"教授没有生气，反而问他："你觉得移民在这里的地位如何？"王磊想了想，干脆回答："比想象中复杂，但值得留下。"

学期结束时，他的论文得了高分。他明白，真正的学习不是背诵理论，而是把知识实践到生活中。德国的社会不完美，却教会他独立思考——这比任何表情包都有意义。
translation: Wang Lei was a Chinese immigrant who had specially moved to Germany three years ago to study sociology. His speaking ability was decent, but his reading ability still needed improvement. Friends around him often said German society was very 'stylish,' yet he felt there was too much theory and too little practice.

One day, he saw a book about East German history in the library. It mentioned that some people had been imprisoned for resisting the government, without any legal grounds. What surprised him more was that the book said pollution had been severe back then, the rivers were unsightly, yet the authorities used meme-like propaganda to cover up the truth.

Wang Lei couldn't help talking back to his professor in the discussion class: 'Isn't this individualism bringing freedom that is actually another form of violence?' The professor wasn't angry; instead, he asked, 'How do you think immigrants' status is here?' Wang Lei thought for a moment and simply replied, 'More complicated than I imagined, but worth staying.'

At the end of the semester, his thesis received a high score. He understood that true learning wasn't memorizing theories, but putting knowledge into practice in life. German society wasn't perfect, but it taught him to think independently—this was more meaningful than any sticker.

title: 德国室友的周末
body:
我的德国室友汉斯是个理论家，总把个人主义挂在嘴边。上周他特意带我去柏林墙遗址，说那里曾关押反抗者的监狱让他思考暴力与自由的关系。我怼他："你们环保实践做得那么差，空气污染这么严重，还好意思谈理想？"他干脆发了个表情包给我，上面写着"你说得对"。

汉斯身边很多朋友都是移民，他发现这些新移民的德语口语能力进步很快，但阅读能力还差得远。有次聚会，一位土耳其移民因为地位低被嘲笑穿着难看、不够洋气，汉斯站出来帮他说话，理由是每个人都该被尊重。这件事让我对他改观不少。

后来汉斯告诉我，他研究社会学的真正动力来自童年。他父亲曾因酒后闹事进过监狱，这段经历带来两种影响：一是让他厌恶暴力，二是让他决心用学术改变社会。现在他的论文专门探讨德国移民政策的矛盾。

上周我生日，他送我一本书，说能同时提高阅读能力和口语能力。封面设计很洋气，内容却讲德国工人如何反抗资本压迫。我笑着说："你这礼物选得真矛盾。"他耸耸肩："生活本身就是矛盾的实践。"
translation: My German roommate Hans is a theorist who always talks about individualism. Last week he specially took me to the Berlin Wall ruins, saying that the prison where resisters were once held made him think about the relationship between violence and freedom. I talked back to him: "Your environmental practice is so poor, air pollution is so serious, and you still have the nerve to talk about ideals?" He simply sent me a meme that said "You're right."

Many friends around Hans are immigrants. He found that these new immigrants' German speaking ability improved quickly, but their reading ability was still far behind. Once at a party, a Turkish immigrant was mocked for his low status, ugly clothes, and lack of Western style. Hans stood up to speak for him, his reason being that everyone deserves respect. This incident changed my view of him considerably.

Later Hans told me that the real motivation for his sociology studies came from childhood. His father once went to prison for causing trouble while drunk. This experience brought two influences: first, it made him hate violence; second, it made him determined to use academia to change society. Now his thesis specifically explores the contradictions in German immigration policy.

Last week for my birthday, he gave me a book, saying it could improve both reading ability and speaking ability at the same time. The cover design was very stylish, but the content was about how German workers resisted capitalist oppression. I smiled and said: "Your gift choice is really contradictory." He shrugged: "Life itself is contradictory practice."

title: 德国的新邻居
body:
去年，我的大学同学小林移民到了德国。他特意选择柏林，因为听说那里环保实践做得很好，空气污染很少。刚到的时候，他的口语能力还不够好，经常听不懂别人说什么，阅读能力也很差，连租房合同都看不懂。

小林发现德国社会很重视个人主义，每个人的地位都由自己的努力决定。有一次，他在地铁上看到有人用暴力对待移民，他很想反抗，却没有理由怼回去，只能默默走开。后来他干脆把这件事做成了表情包，发给身边的朋友，没想到大家反而觉得他很有勇气。

渐渐地，小林身边多了很多德国朋友。他们告诉他，德国的理论教育很强调实践，不会只讲书本知识。虽然有时候德国人的穿着在他看来有点难看，不够洋气，但他学会了尊重不同的文化。

现在小林在一家环保公司工作，把学到的理论都用在实践中。他说德国的社会制度给他带来了很大的改变，让他从一个只会说不敢做的人，变成了敢于表达自己的人。他再也不觉得监狱般的压抑，反而找到了真正的自由。
translation: Last year, my university classmate Xiao Lin immigrated to Germany. He specially chose Berlin because he heard that environmental protection practices were well done there and air pollution was minimal. When he first arrived, his speaking ability was not good enough; he often couldn't understand what others were saying, and his reading ability was so poor that he couldn't even understand rental contracts.

Xiao Lin discovered that German society values individualism highly, and everyone's status is determined by their own efforts. Once, he saw someone using violence against immigrants on the subway; he wanted to resist but had no grounds to talk back, so he could only walk away silently. Later, he simply turned this incident into a meme and sent it to friends around him, unexpectedly everyone thought he was quite courageous instead.

Gradually, many German friends gathered around Xiao Lin. They told him that Germany's theoretical education emphasizes practice greatly and doesn't just teach from books. Although sometimes Germans' clothing looked a bit ugly and not stylish enough in his eyes, he learned to respect different cultures.

Now Xiao Lin works at an environmental protection company, putting all the theories he learned into practice. He says that Germany's social system has brought about great changes in him, transforming him from someone who only talked but dared not act into someone who dares to express himself. He no longer feels the oppression of a prison; instead, he has found true freedom.
